What are the 3 fundamental drivers of AWS Cloud costs?
column2:
1. Compute (hourly/per-second usage)
2. Storage (GB stored, class, requests)
3. Outbound Data Transfer (data OUT to internet or across Regions; data IN is generally free)

column1: How are AWS Data Transfer costs billed (Inbound vs. Outbound vs. Same-AZ vs. Cross-Region)?
column2:
Data IN from internet: Generally FREE.
Data OUT to internet: Charged per GB (tiered discounts for higher volume).
Cross-Region transfer: Charged.
Same-AZ private IP / S3 in same Region: Generally free.

column1: Compare EC2 On-Demand Instances vs. Savings Plans vs. Reserved Instances (RIs).
column2:
On-Demand: Pay per second/hour, zero commitment (short-term, spiky, unpredictable workloads).
Savings Plans: Commit to consistent $/hour spend for 1 or 3 years (up to 66–72% off; Compute SP spans EC2 families, Regions, Fargate & Lambda).
Reserved Instances: Commit to specific instance attributes for 1 or 3 years (up to 72% off; Standard = highest savings; Convertible = change family/OS).

column1: What are the 3 payment options for Reserved Instances & Savings Plans, and which gives the biggest discount?
column2:
1. All Upfront → largest discount (especially on a 3-year term)
2. Partial Upfront → medium discount
3. No Upfront → smallest discount, preserves cash flow

column1: When should you use EC2 Spot Instances, and what is the interruption notice?
column2: Use for stateless, fault-tolerant, flexible, interruptible workloads (batch processing, CI/CD, analytics) for up to 90% discount off On-Demand. AWS can reclaim Spot capacity with a 2-minute interruption notice (no bidding!).

column1: Compare EC2 Dedicated Hosts vs. Dedicated Instances vs. On-Demand Capacity Reservations.
column2:
Dedicated Hosts: Physical server fully dedicated to you with socket/core visibility — best for BYOL per-core/socket compliance.
Dedicated Instances: Runs on single-tenant hardware isolated from other customers, but no host-level visibility.
Capacity Reservations: Reserves EC2 capacity in a specific AZ for any duration (no billing discount by itself, combines with Savings Plans/RIs).

column1: What is the AWS Free Tier (3 offer types)?
column2:
1. Always Free (e.g., Lambda 1M requests/mo, DynamoDB 25 GB)
2. 12 Months Free / Introductory Free Credit for new accounts
3. Short-Term Trials (e.g., 30-day GuardDuty/Macie trials)

column1: What is AWS Organizations Consolidated Billing and its 3 key cost benefits?
column2:
Combines billing for multiple member accounts under one management (payer) account:
1. Single consolidated bill
2. Volume pricing discounts pooled across all accounts (e.g., S3/data transfer tiers)
3. Shared Reserved Instances & Savings Plans unused discounts across accounts

column1: What is AWS Pricing Calculator used for?
column2: Pre-launch cost estimation — model and estimate monthly AWS costs before deploying a new architecture or migrating a workload (replaces the retired Simple Monthly Calculator).

column1: What is AWS Cost Explorer used for?
column2: Interactive console tool to visualize, filter, and analyze historical AWS spend/usage (last 12+ months) and forecast future costs up to 12 months ahead, plus RI/Savings Plan purchase recommendations.

column1: What is AWS Budgets used for?
column2: Set custom cost, usage, RI, or Savings Plan thresholds and trigger automated alerts (email/SNS) or actions when actual or forecasted spend exceeds your budget.

column1: What is the AWS Cost and Usage Report (AWS CUR)?
column2: The most comprehensive, granular line-item billing dataset available in AWS, automatically delivered as CSV/Parquet files to an Amazon S3 bucket for deep analysis in Athena or Amazon Quick.

column1: What are AWS Cost Allocation Tags?
column2: Key-value labels (e.g., CostCenter=Finance, Env=Prod) applied to AWS resources and activated in Billing to track, group, and attribute costs by team, project, or department in Cost Explorer and CUR.

column1: What are AWS Compute Optimizer and AWS License Manager?
column2:
Compute Optimizer: Uses ML to analyze utilization metrics and recommend rightsizing for EC2, EBS, Lambda, and ECS Fargate.
License Manager: Tracks and enforces third-party software licensing rules (BYOL) across AWS and on-premises to prevent compliance violations.

column1: Name the 4 official AWS Support Plans as of 2026 (CLF-C02 Exam Guide v1.3).
column2:
1. Basic Support (Free)
2. AWS Business Support+ ($29/mo min)
3. AWS Enterprise Support ($5,000/mo min)
4. AWS Unified Operations (highest-touch consultative & operational tier)
(Legacy Developer, Business & Enterprise On-Ramp end Jan 1, 2027)

column1: What is included in AWS Basic Support (Free)?
column2: 24x7 access to account and billing support, service quota increases, AWS Support forums, documentation/whitepapers, AWS Health Dashboard, and core Trusted Advisor checks. No technical support cases.

column1: What are the key features and SLA of AWS Business Support+ (2026)?
column2:
Starts at $29/mo min per account:
• Real-time contextual Generative AI support
• 24x7 phone, web, and chat access to Cloud Support Engineers
• < 30 minutes human engagement for business-critical system down
• 500+ AWS Trusted Advisor checks + AWS Support API + third-party software support + unlimited cases

column1: What are the key features and SLA of AWS Enterprise Support (2026)?
column2:
Starts at $5,000/mo min (all Business Support+ benefits plus):
• Designated Technical Account Manager (TAM)
• ≤ 15-minute production-critical response SLA
• AWS Security Incident Response included at no extra cost
• Strategic business reviews & AWS Countdown event management

column1: What distinguishes AWS Unified Operations (2026) from Enterprise Support?
column2: Highest-touch operational plan adding: Designated TAM + Domain Specialist Engineer (DSE), Application Architecture Guidance, Infrastructure Event Management (IEM), recurring AWS Countdown Premium, critical workload reviews, and personalized runbooks.

column1: What are the 6 categories checked by AWS Trusted Advisor?
column2:
1. Cost Optimization
2. Performance
3. Security
4. Fault Tolerance
5. Service Quotas (Limits)
6. Operational Excellence

column1: What is the difference between AWS Health Dashboard, AWS Trust and Safety team, and Service Quotas?
column2:
AWS Health Dashboard: View global AWS service status AND personalized alerts for your account's affected resources (Health API for automation).
AWS Trust and Safety team (legacy: AWS Abuse team): Report suspected abuse or malicious activity originating from AWS resources.
Service Quotas: View and request increases for AWS account resource limits.

column1: Distinguish AWS Knowledge Center, AWS re:Post, AWS Prescriptive Guidance, AWS Professional Services, APN, and AWS Marketplace.
column2:
Knowledge Center: Official AWS FAQ/troubleshooting articles.
re:Post: AWS community Q&A forum.
Prescriptive Guidance: Time-tested migration/modernization patterns.
Professional Services: Paid AWS consultants for hands-on enterprise projects.
APN: Global network of AWS consulting/ISV partners.
Marketplace: Digital catalog to buy/deploy 3rd-party software & SaaS.
